anti_corruption_mechanisms: Header ECC: Hamming-modified (24,8); single-bit-correct + 2-bit-detect over DI + WC of every Packet Header.
Long Packet Checksum: 16-bit CRC, polynomial x^16 + x^12 + x^5 + 1, init 0xFFFF, LSB-first; reports payload corruption (no automatic retransmission).
Sync-pattern lock (D-PHY): receiver only consumes payload after matching 8'b00011101.
EoTp Short Packet (DT=0x08): robust protocol-layer end-of-HS marker decoupling end-of-transmission detection from PHY EoT characteristics.

Acknowledge and Error Report Short Packet (peripheral-sourced DT=0x02): 16-bit error mask reporting SoT / SoT Sync / EoT Sync / Escape Entry / LP TX Sync / HS RX Timeout / False Control / ECC Single / ECC Multi / Checksum / DT Not Recognized / VC ID Invalid / Invalid TX Length / DSI Protocol Violation.
Contention recovery timers (HRX_TO / HTX_TO / LTX-P_TO / LRX-H_TO) provide bounded fault recovery without hard reset (§7.2.2).
LP Contention detector (LP-CD) on bidirectional Data Lane 0 + Annex A recovery flows.
fields.notes: MIPI DSI v1.01.00 provides NO confidentiality, integrity-against-tampering, or authentication features. The wire-level Header ECC, Payload Checksum, EoTp, and Acknowledge-and-Error-Report machinery are noise / bit-error / protocol-fault mitigations only. For content-protection use cases on a display Link (e.g. premium video playback), application-layer security must be layered above DSI; HDCP / DRM and analogous schemes operate above the DSI transport and are NOT part of the DSI specification. For automotive / industrial use cases that require tamper-evident or authenticated display traffic, vendors layer their own extensions (e.g. signed-frame, encryption-at-rest, secure DCS commands) on top of standard DSI Short/Long Packets.
